7; | Mopar ECM T3 SBEC |
8; | Based on 1991 Turbo III Codebase |

10; | Code and original design and data Copyright 1990 by Chrysler Corporation |
11; | This relocateable source is Copyright 2010 by Robert Lloyd |
12; | Modified code modules are Copyright 2010 |
13; | by Robert Lloyd |
14; | 1) Added option config constant for new module options. |
15; | 2) Added switchable boost option, changed code from previous "mod" to |
16; | in-line code; allow for enable/disable by option register. |
17; | 3) Added staging rev limiter (2-step). User can enable/disable in code, or |
18; | by button by the driver, and by speed. |
19; | 4) Added anti-lag code. Pulls timing when transitioning from P/T to WOT |
20; | and while the staging limiter is enabled. |
21; | 5) Added CE Flash for knock indication. CE Light flashes in proportion to |
22; | knock retard.
23; | |
24; | * indicates in progress or planned |
25; \____________________________________________________________________________|

28; History
29;
30; Version 1.0
31; 04/18/11 - Assembles to (nearly) the original binary.
32; - Added basic Turbonator features (CE Flash, Switchable Boost,
33; Staging Limiter, Anti-Lag).
34;
35; 06/06/11 - Converted to MPT2 format (prior to 1st release).
36;
37; Version 1.1
38; 08/04/11 - Added 'TBLBK3_3DTableBreakPointHiLo' to the template. This was
39; previously a declared value in the code that specifies the break
40; point between the hi- and lo-MAP 3D input tables.
41; - Fixed the definitions of 'AVMMAP_MinimumMAPToResetAverageMAP' and
42; 'AVMRPM_MinimumRPMToResetAverageMAP'. They were swapped and
43; 'AVMMAP' was not being scaled correctly for MAP.
44; - Added 'OFSMID_OffsetForMAPOverIdle' to MAP scaling list.
45;
46; Version 1.2
47; 08/09/11 - Updated the Density Factors and MAP-dependant transient fuel
48; tables to scale inversely with MAP.
49; - Updated the naming of the Decel Fuel Shutoff valules and added to
50; a new separate group.
51; - Updated the Staging Limiter code. Was not working due to the decel
52; fuel shutoff code.
53; - Added code to correct the fuel mileage reporting to the CCD bus.
54;
55; Version 1.3
56; 03/07/12 - Updated the template format for improved goruping.
57; Added MP Scan data to the RAM section.
58;

89; *****************************************************************************
90; Calibration Template definition
91; *****************************************************************************
92;
93; This is the calibration template for T-SBEC.
94;
95; This template format will be used from T-SBEC v15 and later.
96;
97; I decided to switch to this format because it was getting clumsy
98; trying to define the switches for all of the build options (MTX/ATX,
99; 2.2/2.5, boost control, etc.). This way, all the calibration data can be
100; kept together in 1 place.
101;
102; T-SBEC and T-SMEC do have compatible template files formats and the 2
103; CAN NOT be interchanged. This is due to the different code structures
104; between the SMEC and SBEC.
105;
106; The relative positions of the data structures should not be changed.
107; But, the calibration values can be changed at will to any value you wish.
108; Or, to match any exsisting calibration.
109;
110; Eventually, I'd like to create a 'new' cal editor that actually edits
111; this tempalte rather than editing the binary file as CHeM and D-Cal
112; currently do.
113;
114; Filename format:
115;
116; T-SBEC_[displ]_[trans]_[ID]_[version].asm
117;
118; For example, the 1st tempalte file I made was from the 89 T1 Auto:
119;
120; T-SBEC_25_ATX_1336.asm
121;
122; This way you can start your T-SMEC build with any calibration. Though,
123; you may have to build a template file if you want a calibration that
124; does not already have a template file.
125;
126

175; ***********************************************************************
176;
177; Bit functions:
178; Many bytes in the RAM contain status bits. For each of these the address value
179; was separated into bit numbers, for example Flags_50 has b50_bit7 through b50_bit0.
180; As the function of the bits was decoded, a global replace was performed to replace
181; the bit name with a meaningful name, like:
182;
183; b50_SparkEngineNotRunning = $%10000000 ; -10000000-
184;
185; When working with bits, you can add several together using the "or" operator | like this:
186;
187; b50_SparkEngineNotRunning | b50_BaroSolEnergized ; -10100000-
188;
189; The inverse function ~ sets all bits except the ones specified, so:
190;
191; ~b50_SparkEngineNotRunning ; -01111111-
192;
193; You can combine the inverse ~ with the or | like this:
194;
195; ~(b50_SparkEngineNotRunning | b50_BaroSolEnergized) ; -01011111-
196;
197; The intent here was to make the logical functionality of the code easier to follow.
198;
199; ***********************************************************************

6057; Staging limiter (2-step) code...
6058;
6059; The staging limiter has 2 activation/deactivation methods.
6060; 1st, the limiter checks to see if it's active by looking for an "enable" switch.
6061; This could be the brake or other input switch. Multiple switches can even be used.
6062; IE, brake + cruise on to enable to staging limiter...
6063; If the switch is "off", then the normal rev limiter values are used.
6064; 2nd, the limiter checks to see if the vehicle speed is above the cutoff point - STGSPD.
6065; If it is, then the normal rev limiter value is loaded.
6066;
6067 
6068 ldx #Turbonator_Flags
6069 ldaa OPTN1_CalCustomOptionConfigFlags1
6070 bita #opt_StageLim
6071 beq Stage_Limiter_Off ;skip looking at the switch state completely if the stage limiter is off
6072 
6073 ; check to see if no switch is selected, if no switch, assume speed cutoff only
6074 ldab STGSWS_StagingLimiterEnableSwitch
6075 beq Stage_Limiter_On
6076 
6077 ldab StartupSwitchMirror1 ; load b with memory contents
6078 bita #opt_StagePol ; check the switch polarity
6079 beq StageLim_Polarity_Lo
6080 
6081StageLim_Polarity_Hi:
6082 bitb STGSWS_StagingLimiterEnableSwitch
6083 beq Stage_Limiter_On ; branch if equal (zero)
6084 bra Stage_Limiter_Off
6085 
6086StageLim_Polarity_Lo:
6087 bitb STGSWS_StagingLimiterEnableSwitch
6088 beq Stage_Limiter_Off
6089 
6090Stage_Limiter_On:
6091 bset 0, x, #Turbonator_Staging ; set the flag to indicate that the staging limiter is active...
6092 ldaa Temp1
6093 cmpa STGSPD_StageLimiterCutoffSpeed ; compare a with memory contents (data is 0a)
6094 bcc Stage_Limiter_Off ; branch if the vehicle speed is greater than the cutoff speed
6095 ldaa STGROF_StageLimiterRPMOffSetpoint ; load a with memory contents (data is 7d)
6096 ldab STGRON_StageLimiterRPMOnSetpoint ; load b with memory contents (data is 77)
6097 bra Store_Limiter_Values ; branch
6098 
6099Stage_Limiter_Off:
6100 bclr 0, x, #Turbonator_Staging ; clear the flag indicating the staging limiter is active...
6101 ldaa REVLMT6_RPMLimiterNormalOffRPM ; load a with memory contents (data is dd)
6102 ldab REVLMT5_RPMLimiterNormalOnRPM ; load b with memory contents (data is d4)

8810Lookup3DTableRoutine:
8811 
8812; The 3D table processing function: Input is 2 8-bit values stored in A and B.
8813; A = Y Axis values, B = X-Axis Values. Output is returned in A.
8814;
8815; The table handles both signed and unsigned data by indicating the type in
8816; the third header byte. It really only makes a small difference to the math.
8817;
8818; Input to table address are in A and B and are values in the range 0-FF.
8819; These values are scaled into the width and height address range of the table
8820; and then used to look up the first byte. The fractional value of the table
8821; column address is retained and used to interpolate between this first byte
8822; and the next byte in the row. The last byte in a row will never be addressed
8823; directly, it's there strictly for the interpolation, which is why you see
8824; the width being DECremented in places. The last row in the table serves a
8825; similar purpose. The process is done a second time at the same column
8826; position, but in the next row down. The two column values derived are then
8827; interpolated between against the fractional Y address, and this value is
8828; returned in A.
8829;
8830;
8831; The data format is pretty simple:
8832;
8833; BYTE 0: Height, number of rows (Y dimension)
8834; BYTE 1: Width, number of columns (X dimension)
8835; BYTE 2: 0 = unsigned data, 80 (Bit 7 set) = signed data
8836;
8837; BYTE 3: Width bytes data
8838; BYTE 3+ (Width *1): Width bytes data
8839; BYTE 3+ (Width *2): Width bytes data
8840; ...
8841; BYTE (3 + Width * Height - 1): Last byte of data
8842 
8843 ; Default is unsigned data
8844 ldY #InterpUnsigned ; load Y index -11010100 10011011-
8845 brclr 2, X, #$%11111111, LD424 ; branch if bit(s) clear
8846 ; Signed data interpolation
8847 ldY #InterpSigned ; load Y index -11010100 10010111-
8848 ; Making room on the stack for local variables
8849 LD424: pshy ; push Y onto stack
8850 psha ; push a onto stack
8851 psha ; push a onto stack
8852 ; Get the number of columns in a row
8853 ldaa 0x01, X ; load a with memory at index + value
8854 ; Decrement because last byte is for interpolation
8855 deca ; decrement a
8856 ; Scale input X value into table X-axis (A), save the fractional part (B) for later
8857 mul ; multiply (d=a*b)
8858 ; A = column number, B = fractional column value for interpolation
8859 psha ; push a onto stack
8860 pshb ; push b onto stack
8861 ; Setup Y to be our frame for local variables on the stack
8862 tSY ; transfer stack to Y
8863 ; Get input row index A value
8864 ldaA 0x02, Y ; load A indexed to Y -00000010-
8865 ; First table byte is number rows in table
8866 ldab 0x00, X ; load b with memory at index + value
8867 ; Decrement because last row is for interpolation only
8868 decb
8869 mul ; multiply (d=a*b)
8870 ; A = row number, B = fractional row value for interpolation
8871 ; Store the fraction for later
8872 staB 0x03, Y ; store B to location indexed to Y -00000011-
8873 ; Get number of columns in table, store for later
8874 ldab 0x01, X ; load b with memory at index + value
8875 staB 0x02, Y ; store B to location indexed to Y -00000010-
8876 ; Multiply row number by the width of a row to get byte-offset into table
8877 mul ; multiply (d=a*b)
8878 ; Bump up X pointer past header to start of data
8879 inx ; increment index (x=x+1)
8880 inx ; increment index (x=x+1)
8881 inx ; increment index (x=x+1)
8882 ; Add offset into table to X
8883 abx ; add b to index
8884 ; If offset is less than 0x100 (IE high byte = 0) then skip next bit
8885 tsta ; test a
8886 beq LD44B ; branch if equal (zero)
8887 ; Add 100H to table offset pointer
8888 ; Note that this effectively limits the table to 0x1ff entries
8889 inx ; increment index (x=x+1)
8890 ldab #0xff ; load b with value -11111111-
8891 abx ; add b to index
8892 ; Get interpolated column position
8893 LD44B: ldaB 0x01, Y ; load B with value indexed to Y -00000001-
8894 ; Add to table offset
8895 abx ; add b to index
8896 ; Get fractional portion of column address
8897 ldaB 0x00, Y ; load B with value indexed to Y -00000000-
8898 ; We need Y for some calcs ahead, save it's value on the stack
8899 pshy ; push Y onto stack
8900 ; Load the pointer to the interpolation entry point chosen at the beginning
8901 ldY 0x04, Y ; load Y indexed to Y -00000100-
8902 ; Get the first data byte indexed from the table
8903 ldaa 0x00, X ; load a with memory at index + value
8904 ; Subtract the next byte in the row
8905 suba 0x01, X
8906 ; Call the interpolator
8907 jsr 0x00, Y ; jump to subroutine at index Y + value -00000000-
8908 ; A contains the return value
8909 ; Restore local variable frame
8910 puly ; pop Y from stack
8911 ; Store interpolated table X value
8912 staA 0x01, Y ; store A with value indexed to Y -00000001-
8913 ; Get number of columns per row
8914 ldaB 0x02, Y ; load B with value indexed to Y -00000010-
8915 ; Advance table offset pointer to next row, same column
8916 abx ; add b to index
8917 ; Get fractional column address from stack
8918 pulb ; pull b from stack
8919 ; Save local variable frame pointer
8920 pshy ; push Y onto stack
8921 ; Get interpolation function pointer
8922 ldY 0x04, Y ; load Y indexed to Y -00000100-
8923 ; Interpolate the value between the two points
8924 ldaa 0x00, X ; load a with memory at index + value
8925 suba 0x01, X
8926 jsr 0x00, Y ; jump to subroutine at index Y + value -00000000-
8927 ; A contains the interpolated value
8928 ; Restore local variable frame
8929 puly ; pop Y from stack
8930 ; X now contains the local variable frame pointer
8931 ; This is done because the interpolation function expects
8932 ; X to point to the two point values, which for this last
8933 ; operation are stored on the stack in our local variable area
8934 tsx ; transfer stack to index (x=sp+1)
8935 ; Store the row+1 interpolated value
8936 staa 0x01, X
8937 ; Get the row address fraction
8938 ldab 0x02, X ; load b with memory at index + value
8939 ; Get the interpolation function pointer
8940 ldY 0x03, X ; load Y indexed to X -00000011-
8941 ; Perform a final interpolation of the values from the two rows
8942 ldaa 0x00, X ; load a with memory at index + value
8943 suba 0x01, X
8944 jsr 0x00, Y ; jump to subroutine at index Y + value -00000000-
8945 ; Clean up stack frame
8946 pulb ; pull b from stack
8947 pulx ; pull index from stack
8948 pulx ; pull index from stack
8949 ; Return value is A
8950 rts ; return from subroutine
8951
8952 ; Appears to be dead code? No references to it I can find
8953 LD489: ldab 0x00, X ; load b with memory at index + value
8954 decb
8955 mul ; multiply (d=a*b)
8956 pshb ; push b onto stack
8957 tab ; b = a
8958 incb
8959 abx ; add b to index
8960 ldd 0x00, X
8961 sba ; subtract (a=a-b)
8962 pulb ; pull b from stack
8963 bra InterpUnsigned ; branch
8964 
8965; This function interpolates the absolute value of the
8966; difference between two points
8967;
8968; Inputs:
8969; A = Delta between two points
8970; B = Fractional value 0-FF
8971; X = Pointer to first point
8972; Carry Flag = Result of Point1 - Point2
8973;
8974; Outputs:
8975; A = interpolated value
8976 
8977 ; Interpolation function, signed math entry point
8978 ; Branch if first byte was less than second
8979 InterpSigned:
8980 blt LD4A3 ; branch if less
8981 bra LD49D ; branch
8982 ; Interpolation function, unsigned math entry point
8983 ; Branch if first byte was less than second
8984 InterpUnsigned:
8985 bcs LD4A3 ; branch if lower
8986 ; First byte was bigger than second
8987 ; Multiply delta x fraction
8988 LD49D: mul ; multiply (d=a*b)
8989 ; Round up
8990 adca #0x00 ; -00000000-
8991 ; Negate result so that value subtracts from first byte
8992 nega ; negate a (set high bit)
8993 bra LD4A7 ; branch
8994 ; Second byte was bigger than first
8995 ; Get abs value of the delta
8996 LD4A3: nega ; negate a (set high bit)
8997 ; Interpolate
8998 mul
8999 ; Round up
9000 adca #0x00 ; -00000000-
9001 ; Add the base value to the interpolated delta value
9002 LD4A7: adda 0x00, X
9003 ; A returns the interpolated value
9004 rts ; return from subroutine

10166; ********************************************************
10167; Scale Y by A, where a=0 = 0.0 and a=255 = 1.0
10168;*************************************************************
10169;
10170; Inputs: A = delta between data and next table point below
10171; Y = 16-bit slope of line
10172;
10173; Outputs:Y = interpolated value
10174;
10175; Pimarily used by the fueling system to calculate an
10176; interpolated point into one of the 5-byte tables. The base
10177; value of the break point will be added to the returned result
10178; of this routine to make the new interpolated return value.
10179;
10180;*************************************************************

10182ScaleYbyA:
10183 psha ; save a copy of the factor on the stack
10184 pshy ; save a copy of the slope on the stack
10185 pulb ; put the high byte of the slope into B
10186 mul ; multiply the delta by the slope high byte
10187 xgDY ; store the 16-bit result from D to Y
10188 pulb ; get the fractional byte of the slope
10189 pula ; retrieve stored copy of the delta
10190 mul ; multiply by the fraction, 16-bit result is D
10191 adca #0x00 ; round off the result with the carry flag
10192 tab ; move A to B
10193 aby ; Add fraction result B to Y
10194 rts ; return from subroutine

10214; ********************************************************
10215; X points to either the MAP or TPS 4-byte block.
10216; block of 4 bytes: x+0: MSB of average value
10217; x+1: LSB of average value (scratch, never used)
10218; x+2: actual value (or faked if limpin)
10219; x+3: scaling factor for leanout or enrichment
10220; flow:
10221; if scaling=0, save value into first byte, zero second, and return
10222; otherwise:
10223; scale average value by scaling factor

10226ProcessMapOrTpsBlockData:

10229 clrb ; b = 0
10230 ldaa 0x02,x ; load a with actual MAP or TPS value
10231 bra L1830 ; store average MAP or TPS value, in this case = same as actual, since the averaging factor = 0
10232 
10233L1829: ldY 0, X ; load Y with the current average MAP or TPS
10234 bsr ScaleYbyA ; scale the average MAP or TPS by the averaging factor
10235 pshy ; push the scaled current average MAP/TPS onto the stack
10236 ldd 0x02,x ; load a with the actual MAP value, b with the averaging factor
10237 mul ; multiply the MAP/TPS by the averaging factor, product ends up in D
10238 tSY ; load Y with the address of the LB of the scaled current average MAP value
10239 subD 0, Y ; subtract scaled current average from the product, delta stays in D
10240 puly ; get scaled current average from the stack (just to clear the stack)
10241 addd 0x00,x ; add the scaled current average to the delta
10242L1830: std 0x00,x ; store the new average to memory
10243 rts ; return from subroutine

12484; ***********************************************************************
12485; ----------------------------------------------------
12486; Additional code modules
12487; ----------------------------------------------------
12488; ----------------------------------------------------
12489; Flash Check Engine Light on Knock Routine
12490; ----------------------------------------------------
12491;
12492; This needs to be called somewhere in the MainProgramLoop,
12493; it is known to work when called at CalcBoostGoal_MM.
12494; PIA1_A_Buffer gets altered throughout the code, every
12495; time through the main loop these bits are copied to the
12496; actual hardware.
12497;
12498; To enable this code, simply check the Custom Options flag for it
12499; in the table file. This codebase has been modified to check for
12500; the option and will automatically re-config the SMEC appropriately.
12501;
12502;
12503UseCELForKnockIndication_MM:
12504 ldx #OPTN1_CalCustomOptionConfigFlags1
12505 brclr 0, X, #opt_FlashCE, FlashCEL_OnKnock_return
12506 brset *BitFlags6d, #b6d_FuelEngineNotRunning, FlashCEL_OnKnock_return ; branch if bit(s) set
12507 ldaa CoolantTemp
12508 cmpa KNKMIN_FlashCEMinTemp
12509 bcs FlashCEL_OnKnock_return; cold motor creates a LOT of false positives
12510 ldaa Cylinder2Retard ; load a with memory contents
12511 bne KnockDetect_LightCEL ; branch if not equal (not zero)
12512 ldaa Cylinder1Retard ; load a with memory contents
12513 bne KnockDetect_LightCEL ; branch if not equal (not zero)
12514 ldaa Cylinder3Retard ; load a with memory contents
12515 bne KnockDetect_LightCEL ; branch if not equal (not zero)
12516 ldaa Cylinder4Retard ; load a with memory contents
12517 bne KnockDetect_LightCEL ; branch if not equal (not zero)
12518NoKnockDetect_UnlightCEL: ; fallthrough, extinguish light
12519 bset *PIA1_Buffer, #pi1_CEL
12520 bra FlashCEL_OnKnock_return
12521KnockDetect_LightCEL:
12522 bclr *PIA1_Buffer, #pi1_CEL
12523FlashCEL_OnKnock_return:
12524 rts
12525;
12526; -------------------------------------------------------
12527; Anti-Lag Retard Routine
12528; -------------------------------------------------------
12529;
12530; This will pull a small amount of timing under specific conditions to
12531; improve turbo spool.
12532;
12533; Timing will normally be pulled when transitioning from P/T to WOT.
12534; But, the transition condition will be ignored if the staging limiter
12535; is active. This will allow the anti-lag to work when staging the car.
12536;
12537; The amount of timing pulled is a function of the difference between
12538; the target boost and the actual MAP reading. This can be tuned via
12539; the lookup table.
12540;
12541; To enable this code, simply check the Custom Options flag for it
12542; in the table file. This codebase has been modified to check for
12543; the option and will automatically re-config the SMEC appropriately.
12544;
12545; Keep in mind, the values from the lookup table will be truncated to the
12546; nearest 0.5 deg when subtracted from the "normal" advance.
12547;
12548CalculateAntiLagRetard_Routine_MM:
12549 ldaa #0x00 ; load 0x00 into A, default anti-lag retard
12550; check that the option is enabled...
12551 ldx #OPTN1_CalCustomOptionConfigFlags1
12552 brclr 0, X, #opt_AntiLag, AntiLag_return
12553; check the conditions for anti-lag - 1st check for staging limiter, then for WOT
12554 ldx #Turbonator_Flags
12555 brset 0, x, #Turbonator_Staging, L3000 ;if the staging limiter is active, ignore WOT requirement
12556 brclr *BitFlags66, #b66_FullThrottle, AntiLag_return
12557L3000:
12558 ldx #ANTLAG_AntiLagRetardfromBoostGoalDelta ; load index with value
12559 ldab 0x01,x ; load minimum Delta MAP reference from the table
12560 addb BaroPressure ; check if MAP is higher than the minimum...
12561 cmpb MapValue
12562 bcc AntiLag_return
12563 ldab BoostTarget ; load the target boost
12564 subb MapValue ; subtract the actual MAP value
12565 bcs AntiLag_return ; branch if greater or equal - no need for antilag
12566 tba
12567 jsr Lookup4ByteTable ; call subroutine
12568 lsra ; divide result by 2
12569 lsra ; divide result by 2
12570 lsra ; divide result by 2
12571 lsra ; divide result by 2
12572 lsra ; divide result by 2 - total dived by 32
12573AntiLag_return:
12574 staa AntiLagRetard ; store the antilag retard
12575 rts
12576;
12577; -------------------------------------------------------
12578; Shift Light Control Routine
12579; -------------------------------------------------------
12580;
12581;
12582; This routine will control a shift light with many parameters
12583; configurable by the user/calibrator.
12584;
12585; Here's how I think this should work:
12586;
12587; 1) 2 setpoints for the shift light; 1 for 1st gear, one for all other gears
12588; 2) adjustable by the driver - special mode?
12589; - special mode: when the engine is not running, press and hold the brake pedal, push cruise set (?) button
12590; - to increment the shift light point; display the value on the tach?
12591; 3) option to flash the light 3 times before the shift, based on rpm
12592; 4) user/calibrator selectable output (cruise solenoids, purge solenoids, egr solenoid, or PTU output, EMR output, etc.)
12593; 5) will require 2 routines; 1 for running the light, the other for setup.
12594;
12595ControlShiftLight_MM:
12596 brclr *Counter_MainLoop, #$%00010000, ShiftLight_Return
12597 ldx OPTN1_CalCustomOptionConfigFlags1
12598 brclr 0, X, #opt_ShiftLight, ShiftLight_Return
12599 brclr *BitFlags6d, #b6d_FuelEngineNotRunning, ShiftLight_Run
12600 
12601ShiftLight_Setup:
12602 ; still need to figure this out...
12603 ;
12604 ; use brake pedal to engage the setup, and the throttle to adjust?
12605 ; press brake pedal 3 times in 2 sec to engage setup (with engine not running, obviously)
12606 ; then press throttle to indicate shift rpm on tach and press brake again to set
12607 ; to set 2nd point, press brake 4 times in 2 sec, otherwise same procedure...
12608 ;
12609 ; need to figure out how to time the tach pulses to do this right, might be difficult to do
12610 ;
12611 ; for testing, I can do this with only constants, not variables...
12612 ; should run with only this line in the "setup" routine...
12613 
12614 bra ShiftLight_Return
12615 
12616ShiftLight_Run:
12617 ldx EngineRpm_HB
12618 cpx SLRPM_ShiftLightSetpoint
12619 bcc ShiftLight_TurnLightOff
12620 
12621ShiftLight_TurnLightOn:
12622 bset *PIA2_Buffer, #pi2_PTU
12623 bra ShiftLight_Return
12624 
12625ShiftLight_TurnLightOff:
12626 bclr *PIA2_Buffer, #pi2_PTU
12627 
12628ShiftLight_Return:
12629 rts

12642; ldaa BatteryVolts ; load a with memory contents

12653; bcs UseMaxDwell ; branch if DWELL+MINADW < DISTPW
12654; ldd MINADW_MinAntiDwellPeriod ; DWELL+MINADW > DISTPW, so use MINADW
